headline: Wall Street Eyes Follow-Through After Monday's Record Run as Iran Uncertainty Lingers
body_html:
Equity futures are pointing to a cautious open on Tuesday after Wall Street's broad Monday rally carried the Dow Jones Industrial Average to a fresh record close, fueled by optimism surrounding ongoing U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks. That optimism, however, faces a live test this morning: a vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, and the status of negotiations remains publicly uncertain, keeping energy markets and safe-haven assets on alert.

Monday's advance was wide and convincing. In our tracked universe of 519 names, 387 issues closed higher against just 132 lower — a nearly three-to-one advance-decline ratio. Materials led all sectors with a gain of 2.35%, followed closely by Industrials at 2.29% and Consumer names at 2.17%. Energy was the lone sector in the red, slipping 0.48% even as crude prices firmed on geopolitical risk.

Today's calendar brings the U.S. jobs report into focus, with gold traders already flagging the data as a key directional trigger. The Federal Reserve's posture on rates — and its potential role in supporting yen stability — adds another layer for macro desks to navigate at the open. Watch oil, the yen, and Treasuries for early tone-setters.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Incident Clouds Iran Talks, Keeps Oil Bid Elevated
briefs.body: A ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, rattling an already fragile diplomatic backdrop as U.S.-Iran talks show no clear resolution. Oil extended gains on the news, with traders citing the strategic chokepoint's sensitivity to any escalation. The development is the primary geopolitical risk to monitor at Tuesday's open.

briefs.headline: BP's Quarterly Profit Surges Past $5 Billion on Oil-Price Tailwind
briefs.body: BP reported that second-quarter net profit more than doubled, crossing the $5 billion threshold as elevated oil prices driven by Middle East conflict boosted upstream revenues sharply. The result lands as a reminder that the same geopolitical tension weighing on risk sentiment is delivering outsized windfalls to major producers. Energy equities will be in focus early.

briefs.headline: Aramco Earnings Climb 44% as Iran War Lifts Crude Benchmarks
briefs.body: Saudi Aramco posted a 44% jump in net profit, attributing the surge directly to higher oil prices stemming from the Iran conflict. The result reinforces the earnings tailwind flowing through the energy complex globally. Analysts will watch whether the OPEC+ production-hike path — currently deemed a near-term non-factor by the group — shifts given these margins.

briefs.headline: Boeing Clears Regulatory Hurdle as FAA Certifies 737 MAX 7
briefs.body: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration granted certification to Boeing's 737 MAX 7 variant, marking a meaningful step forward for the embattled planemaker. The approval expands the deliverable MAX family at a time when Boeing is working to rebuild airline and investor confidence. Shares could see pre-market movement on the news.

briefs.headline: Gold Steady Ahead of Jobs Data as Middle East Risk Supports Demand
briefs.body: Bullion held firm overnight as investors balanced safe-haven demand from Hormuz tensions against anticipation of the U.S. employment report due later today. A stronger-than-expected payrolls print could pressure gold by reinforcing a higher-for-longer rate outlook, while any jobs miss may amplify the geopolitical bid. The metal is a key cross-asset signal at the open.

briefs.headline: Yen Holds Intervention Gains; Fed's Potential Role Draws Scrutiny
briefs.body: The Japanese yen retained ground secured through apparent official intervention, with traders remaining on alert for additional action. A separate analysis flagged the possibility that the Federal Reserve could be drawn into Treasury Secretary Bessent's effort to stabilize the yen — a scenario that would carry significant implications for U.S. monetary policy independence and dollar dynamics.
